To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the jump condition for the temperature profile at the solid–liquid phase boundary in a Maxwell–Cattneao model is the most appropriate boundary condition to use in models of nanopartilce melting and that thermal relaxation is an essential feature in such models.

(i) the jump condition is the most suitable of the boundary conditions for the Maxwell–Cantaneo equation, and (ii) thermal relaxation can significantly increase the time required for nanoparticle melting.

(a) the thermal relaxation time is important for modelling ultrafast nanoparticle melting; (b) the jump boundary condition, not the classical continuity condition, must be used when the Maxwell–Cantaneo equation is employed in phase change modelling; (c) thermal relaxation can increase nanoparticle melting time by more than a order of magnitude.
